title: Lockdown Record
description: What a deadline finalize did to one assignment's cohort, at lockdowns/<assignment-id>/lockdown-record.json. Written whole by lockdown.mjs on every finalize attempt and re-written by the next one, which is why an unlock lives beside it in lockdowns/<id>/unlocked/<login>.json rather than inside it. It is ALSO the idempotency key find-finalizable.mjs reads: a row with a snapshot_sha and no verified preservation re-queues the assignment. This schema was written after the fact - the document had three writers' worth of fields and nothing that could reject one - so every field here was read off lockdown.mjs and off the live records in the participating organizations, and `required` holds only what records written before this schema existed already carry.

deadline_at.description: The ASSIGNMENT's deadline. A student with an extension is deferred instead, and carries their own instant in `deferred_until` on their row.

finalize_attempts.description: First finalize is 1. find-finalizable.mjs stops re-queueing past MAX_FINALIZE_ATTEMPTS so a repository that can never be preserved cannot burn a matrix leg every night.

observer_run.description: The Actions run that wrote this. A debugging aid with a 90-day life on a public repository (ARCHITECTURE §17) - the evidence is this file, not the run.

locked_at.description: When phase 1 fired. Credited to a sentinel's instant where one already stopped the cohort, so uncertainty_seconds stays honest.

lock_method.description: What the run set out to do for the cohort. A row may differ from it: a ruleset that could not be applied degrades to a demotion for that repository alone, so the ROW's lock_method is what an unlock reads. NOT required: PXL-Systems-Expert's two 2026 records predate the field, and refusing them would make this schema a claim about documents it cannot fix.

org_ruleset_id.description: The organization ruleset covering this cohort, when lock_method is `org-ruleset`. A convenience for reading; never the lookup key. The sentinel's STOP_ONLY path writes no record at all, so at the moment it fires there is no stored id - findOrgSubmissionLock resolves by NAME, and this field only saves a call afterwards.

no_submission_count.description: Branches holding nothing committed before the student's deadline. Under `block` that is an outcome, not a failure, and preserve treats it as its own bucket.

deferred_count.description: Left alone because a granted extension is still running. Neither a lock nor an error, so the run stays green.

reopened_count.description: Deliberately reopened by a lecturer and therefore not re-locked by this pass. Counted apart from deferrals and errors because it is neither: nothing failed and nobody was granted more time. These produce no result row - the count is the record.

unfreezable_count.description: Accounts that own the organization and keep admin whatever the run does. Not an error: nothing can freeze them under a demotion, and a ruleset stops them anyway.

results.description: One row per LOGIN, not per repository - a group assignment's five members share one repository and produce five rows naming it.

repo_name.description: `owner/name`, because a record nothing regenerates has to be readable with no other document beside it.

repo_id.description: The immutable id (§13). What an organization ruleset targets, and what survives a rename.

snapshot_sha.description: The submission. Frozen on retry: a later attempt reuses this rather than re-reading HEAD, or a late push would replace the on-time submission. Null with a `deferred_until` means deferred, and null WITHOUT one is a lockdown failure - preserve tells them apart on exactly that.

pushed_at.description: GitHub's own server-side timestamp for the last push. Unlike a commit date, a student cannot set it - the one field here they cannot influence.

lock_method.description: What actually stopped THIS repository, which is not always what the run set out to do. lib/repo-unlock.mjs reads it to pick the inverse: undoing a demotion with a ruleset flip reports success over a student who still cannot push.

reconstructed.description: The submission was rebuilt with `?until=` rather than read off HEAD, because a push landed after the deadline. Committer-date based, and that date is client-supplied.

permission_after.description: Read back after the demotion, never assumed. `admin` here beside verified:false is an organization owner, who cannot be demoted at all.

verified.description: Whether the lock was confirmed, not whether the call returned 2xx.

unfreezable_reason.description: Why this one was not frozen. Recorded rather than inferred from permission_after, because `admin` is also what a transient failure leaves behind and a grade dispute should not turn on somebody re-deriving the difference months later.

uncertainty_seconds.description: How long after THIS student's deadline they could still push - not after the assignment's.

reopened_at.description: When a lecturer reopened this repository, copied from lockdowns/<id>/unlocked/<login>.json at the pass that skipped it. A reopened student used to be DROPPED from this record entirely - the run counted them in reopened_count and then wrote nothing about them, so the document a grade dispute reads lost the fact that they were ever locked. A deferred student has always kept a row saying why; this is the same answer for the other reason a repository is not locked. lock_method is null on such a row, because nothing is holding it now.
